text:
maria: Heads up — after yesterday's kernel-selector push to heuristic-v2 we're seeing a regression on MoE routes on 8xA100 rigs. Throughput down ~18% on long sequences, latency tail up.

chris: Oof. Any traces or flamegraphs yet?

maria: Not uploaded centrally. I ran a quick nsys capture on a dev rig (seq=2048, batch=32, 4 experts) — big gaps during token routing phase. Looks like more time in all-to-all + waiting on all-reduce than before.

sven: I pulled that capture. Early impression: kernel-selector picked fallback GEMM kernels for the expert FFNs for some tile shapes. That + larger all2all sizes (due to increased token fanout) means reduced comm/compute overlap.

leah: KV cache telemetry shows per-token fanout distribution shifted right after the change — median fanout unchanged but 95th/99th increased. So same hit rate, but more tokens routed to many experts. Could be batching heuristic interaction.

maria: Repro steps I used: 
```
python -m infra.run_bench --model moe_16e --gpus 8 --seq 2048 --batch 32 --kernel_selector heuristic-v2 --kv_cache=true
nsys profile -o /tmp/nsys.moe ./run_bench.sh
```

sven: From nsys timeline: long NCCL AllToAll + NCCL AllReduce blocks starting at token 1200..2000. Compute kernels for experts are short but not enough to hide comm. Also saw a dozen launches of a slower GEMM variant: `expert_ffn_gemm_fallback_v1` instead of `expert_ffn_opt_v3`.

chris: Do we have kernel selection mapping logs? Maybe heuristic-v2 changed threshold for using opt_v3 for odd tile sizes.

maria: Yes. The selector added a heuristic for memory pressure vs. occupancy that tips to fallback for tiles < 64x64 on Ampere, but our expert dims sit near that boundary.

leah: That explains it. If more experts pick the fallback, compute per-expert gets slower -> less overlap -> allreduce shows up. Also the batching heuristic increase in max_batch_tokens last week made the all2all payloads larger (we pack more sequences before cut).

perf-bot: perf-report: 
- throughput baseline (old selector): 103.2 tok/s per GPU
- current (heuristic-v2): 84.6 tok/s per GPU
- NCCL allreduce median latency: 0.9ms -> 2.6ms
- 99th token fanout: 12 -> 18

chris: Nice summary. Options: revert kernel-selector change, tighten heuristics (prefer opt_v3 for these dims), or cap batching to keep all2all payloads smaller. Which rollback is least risky?

sven: Short term: revert kernel-selector on the fleet canary and run targeted tests. Medium: add a kernel-mapping override table for MoE expert shapes to force opt_v3. Long: adjust batching to be workload-aware (limit tokens-per-all2all based on fanout distribution).

maria: Proposed immediate actions:
- sven: revert selector on canary cluster and run same nsys job (ETA 1h)
- leah: push a KV-cache telemetry patch to record per-request fanout histogram (ETA today)
- chris: add a tiny canary job that varies max_batch_tokens (32k/64k/96k) to map throughput vs all2all size (ETA tomorrow)

leah: I'll also add a quick dashboard tile for expert kernel variant counts (opt_v3 vs fallback) per model so we can correlate.

perf-bot: noted: created perf-incident-1999, attached current traces at s3://redwood-perf/moe/1999123456/*.npy

maria: Thanks. If revert proves clean we'll do a staged rollback. If not, we'll apply the mapping override for the most common expert dims and then iterate on batching heuristics. :thumbsup:

chris: ping me when canary results are in, I'll run a couple of production-like workloads against it.

sven: starting the canary revert now — will post logs once nsys profiles finish.

maria: Appreciate it. Keeping this thread for updates so we don't lose the traces.

(ended)
